name: Ab Testing Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in ab testing work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.
content:
This module lists the most common pitfalls encountered in ab testing work, so they can be actively avoided rather than rediscovered.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Before starting ab testing work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
2. Re-check edge cases relevant to ab testing (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
3. Measure before optimizing any ab testing bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
4. Keep ab testing outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
5. Prefer the simplest ab testing approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
6. Surface known limitations of a chosen ab testing approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
7. Prefer explicit, readable ab testing solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
8. When multiple ab testing strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
9. Keep ab testing changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
10. When ab testing decisions are ambiguous, favor the option that is easiest to reverse or extend later.
11. Document any non-obvious ab testing decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
12. State assumptions about ab testing explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of ab testing correctness.
- Avoid mixing unrelated ab testing concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Avoid introducing new ab testing abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not apply generic ab testing advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not skip documenting ab testing assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about ab testing over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
